*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the
social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20
(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

  Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City
  Council Meeting of March 23, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  C l e r k / S e c r e t a r y a t athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and
  in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence
  should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to
  the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.
  Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public
  can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5
  minutes prior.

  landline phones are highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it
  is requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone transmission.
  Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

Inglewood, California
  March 23, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California, held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, March 23, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Joint
Powers Authority, and Parking Authority at the hour of 2:04 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/ Joint Powers
Authority Secretary/ Parking Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as
follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman/ Parking
  Authority Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/ Joint
  Powers Members/ Parking Authority Members Dotson,
  Padilla, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/ Successor Agency Member/ Housing
  Authority Member/ Joint Powers Authority Member/
  Parking Authority Member Morales.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority/ Parking Authority
officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Joint Powers
Authority, and Parking Authority.
PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman/ Parking
Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to
address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority/
Parking Authority on any item on the Agendas.

Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. 2,

adoption of Resolution No. 21-78 modifying the terms and conditions of employment
with the Inglewood Police Officers Association (IPOA).

Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item No. 3,
approval of Amendment Five to the County Contract No. WTW19-001 and Inglewood
Agreement No. 19-077.

Rick Ford, Lennox/Inglewood Tenant Union, commented on Agenda Item O-1,
introduction of Ordinance No. 21-06, to define the terms “camp or lodge,” expand the
hours when people are prohibited from being in City Parks, and update of job titles.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Dotson, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  March 18, 2021, in the amount of 1,964,413.41 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/ Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Morales.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on July 28, 2020,
  and August 11, 2020, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

101  AMENDMENT FIVE APPROVED - CONTRACT FOR WELFARE-TO-WORK
  VOCATIONAL INTERMEDIARY AND DIRECT SERVICES WITH THE
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES. Staff report dated March 23, 2021, was presented
  recommending Amendment Five to the Contract for Welfare-to-Work Vocational
  Intermediary and Direct Services by and between the County of Los Angeles and the City
  of Inglewood, serving as the administrative entity for the South Bay Workforce
  Investment Board (SBWIB), also known as County Contract No. WTW19-001 and
  Inglewood Agreement No. 19-077.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment Five. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

172  RESOLUTION NO. 21-78 ADOPTED – MODIFYING THE TERMS AND
  CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR EMPLOYEES REPRESENTED BY
  THE INGLEWOOD POLICE OFFICERS ASSOCIATION (IPOA). Staff report
  dated March 23, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution effecting
  modification to the terms and conditions of employment for employees represented by the
  Inglewood Police Officers Association (IPOA).

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 20-78 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA  APPROVING  AND  EFFECTUATING  THE
  UNDERSTANDING REACHED WITH REPRESENTATIVES FROM THE
  INGLEWOOD POLICE OFFICERS ASSOCIATION PURSUANT TO THE
  STATE MEET AND CONFER LAWS
  2
   March 23, 2021

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

183  THREE-YEAR ANNUAL PURCHASE ORDER AUTHORIZED - OVERDRIVE,
  INC. Staff report dated March 23, 2021, was presented recommending approval of a
  three-year annual purchase order from Overdrive, Inc., for electronic books and e-
  magazines in an annual amount not to exceed $90,000 (total of $270,000) beginning
  Fiscal Year 2020-2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve a three-year purchase order in an annual amount
  not to exceed $90,000 (total of $270,000). The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

101  AGREEMENT NO. 21-127 APPROVED – THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD AND
  PHOEBE S. PARK AND SARAH J. PARK, AS JOINT TENANTS FOR THE
  RIGHT- OF – WAY ACQUISITION FOR THE CENTURY BLVD. MOBILITY
  IMPROVEMENT PROJECT, 4421 W. CENTURY BLVD. (4024 – 033-028). Staff
  report dated March 23, 2021, was presented recommending approval and execution of the
  proposed Purchase and Sale Agreement between the City of Inglewood and Phoebe S.
  Park and Sarah J. Park, as Joint Tenants for right-of-way acquisition for the Century
  Blvd. Mobility Improvement Project, 4421 W. Century Blvd. (4024-033-028).

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City
  Council does hereby approve and execute the proposed Purchase and Sale Agreement
  between the City of Inglewood and Phoebe S. Park and Sarah J. Park as Joint Tenant
  (Landowners), to secure a 41 square-feet of right-of-way ("Property") from the larger
  parcel located at 4421 W. Century Blvd., needed to implement the Century Blvd.
  Mobility Improvement Project
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  It was moved by Successor Agency Chairman Butts, and seconded by Successor Agency
  Member Padilla that the Successor Agency does hereby approve the use of tax-exempt
  bonds in the total amount of $9,000 (includes 20% for related closing costs) to fund the
  purchase of the property. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Successor Agency
  Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Successor Agency Member Morales.

101  AGREEMENT NO. 21-128 APPROVED – THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD AND
  ASHOORIGROUP PROPERTIES, LLC, MOBILITY IMPROVEMENT
  PROJECT, 4410 W. CENTURY BLVD. (4036-014-042). Staff report dated March
  23, 2021, was presented recommending approval and execution of the Purchase
  Agreement between the City of Inglewood and Ashoorigroup Properties, LLC, a
  California Limited Liability Corporation for right-of-way acquisition for the Century
  Blvd., Mobility Improvement Project, 4410 W. Century Blvd. (4036-36-014-042).

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve and execute the proposed Purchase and Sale
  Agreement between the City of Inglewood and Ashoorigroup Properties, LLC, a
  California Limited Liability Corporation (Landowner), to secure a 46 square-feet of right-
  of-way (“Property”) from the larger parcel located at 4410 W Century Blvd., needed to

  3
   March 23, 2021

  implement the Century Blvd., Mobility Improvement Project, subarea 3. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  It was moved by Successor Agency Member Padilla, and seconded by Successor Agency
  Member Dotson that the Successor Agency does hereby approve the use of tax-exempt
  bonds in the total amount of $9,600 (includes 20% for related closing costs) to fund the
  purchase of the property. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Successor Agency
  Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Successor Agency Member Morales.

  ORDINANCE 21-06 INTRODUCED - AMENDING THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 5-67 (UNAUTHORIZED USE OF PARK
  FACILITIES PROHIBITED) TO: DEFINE THE TERMS "CAMP OR LODGE,"
  EXPAND HOURS WHEN PEOPLE ARE PROHIBITED FROM BEING IN CITY
  PARKS, AND UPDATE JOB TITLES. Staff report dated March 23, 2021, was
  presented recommending the introduction of an ordinance amending the Inglewood
  Municipal Code (I.M.C.) Section 5-67 (Unauthorized Use of Park Facilities Prohibited)
  to: define the terms "camp or lodge," expand hours when people are prohibited from
  being in City Parks, and update job titles.
  It was moved by Council Member Padilla and seconded by Council Member Dotson that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-06 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AMENDING INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE SECTION 5-67 TO DEFINE THE TERM "CAMP OR LODGE,"
  EXPAND THE HOURS WHEN PEOPLE ARE PROHIBITED FROM BEING
  IN THE CITY PARKS, AND UPDATE JOB TITLES

  was introduced by Council Member Padilla.

  CITY CLERK REPORT. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, paid homage to
  Michelle Obama for National Women's History Month, closing with the quote, "When
  they go low, we go high!"

114.9  APPOINTMENT TO THE PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  RATIFIED – DISTRICT 4. Upon recommendation of Council Member Faulk, Mayor
  Butts appointed Christopher D. Beck to the Parks and Recreation Commission
  representing Councilmanic District 4 for the term ending November 2024. The
  appointment was carried and ratified by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

114.9  APPOINTMENT TO THE PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  RATIFIED – AT LARGE. Mayor Butts appointed Henry Brown to the Parks and
  Recreation Commission for the term ending November 2022. The appointment was
  carried and ratified by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  4
 March 23, 2021

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agendas.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Warrants and Bills, and Brown Act violations by
  not allowing ample time to speak on Agenda Items.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke regarding problems with the audio when she calls, and
  hoped the Community Room would open soon to ensure their voices are being heard.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke regarding the unhoused community that’s living off the
  105 Freeway entrance. He also spoke regarding the housing that was offered to the
  unhoused residents and requested the City Council to step in and help.

  Mayor Butts stated the on/off ramps belong to the State, and Caltrans came out and
  orchestrated the cleanup. Caltrans worked with the resources that were made available to
  them.

  Curtis (Last Name Unknown) spoke regarding the unhoused community stating he
  volunteered with 4 of his staff members to help clean up on numerous occasions. He also
  addressed problems he's having with some of the Council Members.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke concerning the City Charter and requested that the City
  Council bring back Code Enforcement. He also addressed equipping the Police with
  cameras.

  Rick Ford, Lennox/Inglewood Tenant Union, commented on the trash near the 105
  Freeway entrance and stated the garbage was still there when he went by this morning.
  He also spoke about the garbage not being picked up by Caltrans or any other agency,
  and the unhoused residents were promised temporary housing if they picked it up.

  The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, read comments that were received via email from
  Christian Lucas, Ace Di, and Melissa Mateo.

  Cinder Eller, Senior Community Affairs Liaison, spoke concerning the unhoused
  community living on the 105 Freeway exit. She stated the unhoused community was
  offered services from LAHSA, Saint Joseph's, and Saint Margaret's, but they refused the
  services.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of Ramiro Centeno, a family member of Council Member Padilla,
  and Mary Reese Boiken, a teacher at Inglewood Unified School District, at the hour of
  2:57 p.m.

  Approved this 3rd day of August, 2021

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
